title: G-Drive wins at Silverstone from Panis Barthez pole
dek: Roman Rusinov, Andrea Pizzitola and Jean-Eric Vergne won from second on the grid, a lap clear of DragonSpeed, to give G-Drive a third straight win and a 34-point lead.

chapters.title: A double-header on a new surface
text: The 4 Hours of Silverstone on 18 August 2018 was the fourth of six European Le Mans Series rounds and one half of a double-header, with the FIA World Endurance Championship's Six Hours following on the same circuit the next day. That squeezed the teams doing both: DragonSpeed, Gulf Racing, TDS Racing and Proton Competition split crews and equipment between two pit lanes, and DragonSpeed's Elton Julian called it the biggest operation his team had ever run, with a rehearsed golf-cart dash between the paddocks. In LMP2 the entry was a big one, 16 cars on the grid out of 41 starters in all.

G-Drive Racing arrived as championship leader. Its TDS-run Oreca #26 had won at Monza and again at the Red Bull Ring, while Racing Engineering had opened the season with a win on its series debut at Le Castellet. There were line-up changes at the front. Matthieu Vaxiviere took the third seat in the Racing Engineering Oreca #24 in place of Olivier Pla, who was due back at Spa, and Garry Findlay returned to the series in the second G-Drive car, the #40.

The circuit itself was the main talking point. Silverstone had been resurfaced earlier in the year, and Dunlop's technicians described a smoother track overall but one with short, sharp bumps at the entry to Maggotts and at Stowe that unsettled cars under braking, little drainage in the wet, and a darker surface that held heat, adding perhaps 10 to 15 degrees to track temperatures on a 30-degree day. Sharper kerb edges also made cutting corners a tyre risk. On Friday the Dunlop-shod G-Drive Oreca set the pace in both sessions, with Vergne's 1:45.490 in the afternoon seven-tenths clear of Ben Hanley's DragonSpeed car, which was second in both.

chapters.title: Stevens takes a surprise pole
text: Michelin runners had not been expected to trouble G-Drive, but Will Stevens put the Panis Barthez Competition Ligier JS P217 on pole with a late 1:43.690, 0.736 seconds quicker than Vergne's 1:44.426 in the #26 Oreca. It was the first pole of 2018 for a JS P217, and it came for a Michelin-shod car against a Dunlop-shod Oreca that had topped both practice sessions. "It's a great feeling to score a pole at home," Stevens said, adding that the team had known since Friday it had a strong package.

Hanley put the DragonSpeed Oreca #21 third on 1:44.539, ahead of Nicolas Jamin's Duqueine Engineering #29 and James Allen in the second G-Drive car, the #40, in fourth and fifth. Anders Fjordbach was the best of the Dallaras in sixth in the High Class Racing #49, with Nato seventh for Racing Engineering and Paul Loup Chatin eighth for IDEC Sport. The United Autosports Ligiers were well down the order, Wayne Boyd tenth in the #32 and Filipe Albuquerque twelfth in the #22.

In the support classes, Eurointernational's Mattia Drudi took LMP3 pole by 0.046 seconds from Ross Kaiser's 360 Racing car, and Dennis Olsen put the Proton Competition Porsche #77 on LMGTE pole, 0.060 ahead of his team-mate Matteo Cairoli.

chapters.title: Canal leads, Rusinov waits
text: With 41 cars on the grid, Julien Canal kept the Panis Barthez Ligier ahead of Rusinov into the first corner, but the start was messy further back. Several cars were forced off into the Village complex, among them the Cetilar Villorba Corse Dallara #47, which dropped far down the order and completed only 98 laps, and the Duqueine #29.

Canal led for the first hour with Rusinov at his tail, the pair working through backmarkers together. Roughly an hour in, Rusinov found a way past on the outside and took the lead for G-Drive, a position the #26 would not lose for the rest of the afternoon.

chapters.title: Two retirements and a Full Course Yellow
text: Early in the second hour the United Autosports Ligier #22 stopped at Village, with Phil Hanson climbing out after the car's fire extinguisher went off and shut down its systems. Moments later the SMP Racing Dallara #35 went off at the same spot and was too damaged to continue. Neither car was classified, and the Full Course Yellow that followed while the cars were recovered let most of the LMP2 field make a third stop and change drivers.

By the end of the second hour Pizzitola led comfortably from Timothe Buret in the Panis Barthez Ligier and Henrique Chaves in the AVF Dallara #30. Vergne took over in the third hour and began stretching the gap, while DragonSpeed's Henrik Hedman lost several places in a short space of time. Behind the leaders there was plenty of contact in the midfield, with the APR-Rebellion Oreca involved in several incidents.

chapters.title: Nato goes off, the order thins out
text: With the final hour under way Vergne was well clear, and the race was being decided for the places behind him. The AVF Dallara #30 dropped away when it came in for a new rear wing, a stop that left it eighth at the flag. Norman Nato had been in the thick of the podium fight in the Racing Engineering Oreca #24, but he went off around lap 110, 18 laps from the end, and the car did not return, leaving it unclassified.

chapters.title: A lap clear, with a late shuffle behind
text: Vergne took the chequered flag after 128 laps, a full lap clear of the field, and set the fastest lap of the race on the way, a 1:47.225. The fight for the other two podium places was settled in the last few minutes. Paul Lafargue was running second in the IDEC Sport Oreca #28 but had to stop for a splash of fuel with fewer than ten minutes left, which let Nicolas Lapierre, who had taken over the DragonSpeed car for the final stint and had been climbing the order, through for second. IDEC took third on the same lap.

Graff's Oreca was fourth, and the APR-Rebellion Oreca fifth, a lap down, after a race of contact that included a coming-together with the Panis Barthez Ligier. That car, which had started on pole, finished sixth, ahead of the Duqueine in seventh and the AVF Dallara in eighth.

chapters.title: A third straight win and a bigger lead
text: It was a third consecutive ELMS victory for Rusinov, Pizzitola and Vergne, and it stretched G-Drive's lead in the championship to 34 points over Racing Engineering with two rounds to go. Nato's off had cost the Spanish team a strong finish at the worst moment. For DragonSpeed, Lapierre had a strong weekend, completing podiums in both the ELMS and WEC races at the circuit within 24 hours.

The win came with a shadow over it. The same three drivers had taken the LMP2 class victory at the Le Mans 24 Hours in June only to be excluded for a refuelling violation, and the FIA Court of Appeal was due to hear the case the following month. Rusinov also said he could return to the WEC at the 1000 Miles of Sebring in March.

For the home teams it was a mixed day. Stevens's pole was the first of the season for a JS P217, but the Panis Barthez car finished sixth, and United Autosports left LMP2 with a tenth place and a retirement. Panis Barthez Competition and Graff, which finished fourth here, both said afterwards that they were weighing entries at the 2019 Daytona 24 Hours. Gibson also marked a milestone over the weekend, with its LMP2 engines passing one million kilometres of track use since their debut in September 2016.
The next round of the European Le Mans Series is at Spa-Francorchamps on 23 September, with Pla due to return to the Racing Engineering line-up.

facts.v: Will Stevens put the Panis Barthez Ligier on pole with 1:43.690, 0.736 seconds clear of Vergne's G-Drive Oreca.
